record.paper_title: Noncommutative spectral geometry of Riemannian foliations: some results and open problems
record.original_question: For the noncommutative algebra C^infinity_prop(G_FN, |T G_N|^{1/2}) associated with the linearized foliation on the conormal bundle of a Riemannian foliation, can one define a notion of noncommutative Hamiltonian flow such that the transverse Hamiltonian flows constructed from homogeneous degree-one Hamiltonians become examples of noncommutative Hamiltonian flows?

evidence.quote: Block and Getzler [4] defined a Poisson structure on the operator algebra C_c^infinity(G, |T G|^{1/2}) of a transversally symplectic foliation... A natural example ... is given by the linearized foliation F_N on the conormal bundle N^*F to a Riemannian foliation F. So the construction of Block and Getzler can be applied in this case, and we get a natural noncommutative Poisson structure on C^infinity_prop(G_FN, |T G_N|^{1/2}).

Problem 4.6. To define the notion of noncommutative Hamiltonian flow on a noncommutative algebra so that the transverse Hamiltonian flows on C^infinity_prop(G_FN, |T G_N|^{1/2}) would be noncommutative Hamiltonian flows.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,F)$ be a Riemannian foliation on a smooth compact manifold, and let $N^*F \subset T^*M$ be its conormal bundle. The lifted (linearized) foliation $F_N$ on $N^*F$ carries a natural transverse symplectic structure, and its holonomy groupoid $G_{F_N}$ has a tangent half-density bundle $|TG_N|^{1/2}$. Consider the convolution algebra $\mathcal{A} = C^\infty_{\mathrm{prop}}(G_{F_N}, |TG_N|^{1/2})$ of properly supported smooth half-densities on $G_{F_N}$. By the Block–Getzler construction applied to the transversely symplectic foliation $(N^*F, F_N)$, the algebra $\mathcal{A}$ carries a canonical noncommutative Poisson structure, i.e. a Lie bracket $\{\cdot,\cdot\}$ on $\mathcal{A}/[\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}]$ (or equivalently a derivation $\{a,\cdot\}$ for each class $[a]$). Moreover, every smooth function $H$ on $N^*F$ that is invariant along the leaves of $F_N$ and homogeneous of degree one in the cotangent fibers determines a transverse Hamiltonian flow on $(N^*F, F_N)$, which in turn induces a one-parameter group of automorphisms of $\mathcal{A}$.

Problem. Formulate a notion of "noncommutative Hamiltonian flow" on a noncommutative Poisson algebra (in the sense of Block–Getzler–Xu) — that is, a definition of a one-parameter group of automorphisms generated, in an appropriate sense, by an element (or class) of the algebra via the noncommutative Poisson bracket — such that the transverse Hamiltonian flows on $\mathcal{A} = C^\infty_{\mathrm{prop}}(G_{F_N}, |TG_N|^{1/2})$ coming from the leafwise-invariant, fiberwise degree-one homogeneous Hamiltonians on $N^*F$ are examples of noncommutative Hamiltonian flows in this sense.
artifact.status_search_result: A subsequent work titled "Noncommutative Hamiltonian dynamics on foliated manifolds" (J. Fixed Point Theory Appl. 7 (2010), 385–399) introduces a notion of Hamiltonian vector field on a noncommutative Poisson algebra in the Block–Getzler–Xu sense and constructs a class of Hamiltonian vector fields on the noncommutative algebra associated with a transversely symplectic foliation. This addresses the infinitesimal (Hamiltonian vector field) version of the problem; the integration of these vector fields to bona fide noncommutative Hamiltonian flows realizing the transverse Hamiltonian flows from homogeneous degree-one Hamiltonians appears to be only partially established.

status_evidence.title: Noncommutative Hamiltonian dynamics on foliated manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: reviews the notion of a Poisson structure on a noncommutative algebra due to Block, Getzler and Xu, and introduces a notion of a Hamiltonian vector field on a noncommutative Poisson algebra... describes a Poisson structure on a noncommutative algebra associated with a transversely symplectic foliation and constructs a class of Hamiltonian vector fields
status_evidence.claim: Defines noncommutative Hamiltonian vector fields and applies them to transversely symplectic foliations, partially addressing the problem.

status_evidence.title: Quantization of foliations (Block–Getzler)
status_evidence.snippet: Poisson structure on the operator algebra of a transversally symplectic foliation
status_evidence.claim: Provides the noncommutative Poisson structure used in the problem setup.
